This claim petition is filed by the petitioners under Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988 seeking compensation for the death of Imran Pasha caused in a road traffic accident.

2. The facts leading to the filing of top noted petition are that on 2-9-2021 when Imran Pasha was riding the Honda activa scooter bearing reg.No.KA-06-EZ-3339 on extreme left side on Tumkur-Gubbi NH 206 road slowly and cautiously at about 10.50 a.m. near MH Patna bus stop,
Gubbi Taluk, Tumkur, at that time, driver of the Milk tanker bearing reg.No.KA-07-A-2986 came from Gubbi side in a rash and negligent manner endangering to human life without observing any traffic rules and regulations and dashed against the honda activa, due to which Imran Pasha fell down along with vehicle and sustained grievous injuries and succumbed to the injuries on the spot.
Immediately after the accident, Imran Pasha was shifted to Gubbi Govt., hospital wherein post mortem was conducted and shifted the dead body to his residence and spent Rs.1 lakh for funeral,
obsequies ceremonies.
Prior to the accident, deceased was hale and healthy and working as driver and earning Rs.20,000/-p.m. and deceased was the only earning member in the family.
Due to sudden demise of the deceased, petitioner lost the love and affection and earning member of the family.
Hence prays to award compensation of Rs.30 lakhs.
3. After service of notice to respondents, the respondent No.1 remained exparte.
The respondent No.2 filed written statement wherein contended that police after thorough investigation filed the charge sheet against the rider of 2 wheeler/deceased.
In the charge sheet it is specifically mentioned that the deceased came from opposite e direction on the right side and dashed to the milk tanker.

As per the sketch the deceased himself came to the wrong side of the road rash and negligently and dashed to the milk tanker, there is no fault or rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of milk tanker.
Further deceased was not having DL, policy for two wheeler and also not wearing helmet.
If the deceased was to be careful and vigilant he could have avoided the accident.

The owner of the milk tanker has not immediately reported the occurrence of the accident to this respondent and has not immediately submitted the claim form and other documents like RC, FC, permit and DL etc., for verification.
The driver of the milk tanker was driving the vehicle without possessing a valid and effective DL, FC, permit.
There is violation of policy conditions.
The compensation claimed by the petitioner is highly excessive, arbitrary and disproportionate.
Hence prays to dismiss the petition.

4. On the basis of the above pleadings this tribunal has framed the following issues :
ISSUES Zareena Taj vs Sudha.

chest, legs and body and there was severe bleeding and he died on the spot and Honda Activa bearing reg.No.KA-06-EZ-3339 was completely damaged.
Thereafter he called for the ambulance and taken the deadbody to the government hospital and informed about the accident to his family
Further stated that the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the milk tanker bearing reg.No.KA-07-A-2986 and prays to take legal action against him.
Accordingly the jurisdictional police have registered the FIR as per Ex-P1 against the driver of the milk tanker.

15. But as argued by the respondent counsel, the jurisdictional police have filed the charge sheet against the deceased Imran Pasha by holding that on that day, accident had been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver Imran Pasha and as Imran Pasha drove the vehicle to the right side and hit to the milk tanker coming from the Gubbi, accident had been taken place and filed the abated charge sheet.

But however mere filing of the charge sheet against the deceased itself cannot be considered as a conclusive proof as to rash and negligent driving as rightly argued by the counsel for the petitioner.

16. At this juncture, it is relevant to refer to an unreported judgment in MFA No.201689/2016 (MV)
Mahadevi & Ors., Vs. Shivaputra & Anr.

Wherein it was observed that "there is no law laid down in the said judgment of universal application that in all cases where charge sheets were filed, unless Insura nce Company challenges the same and obtains writ of mandamus, MACTs are required to act upon the same and proceed to come to a conclusion that the vehicles named as offending vehicles in the charge sheet, without any further proof, are to be taken as the motor vehicles involved in causing the accident, even in cases where evidence produced points to the contrary".

17. Even the said Mahamad Nayaz Ulla eye witness to the accident was examined by the petitioner as PW-2 who has clearly deposed about the witnessing of the accident and the cause and manner of the accident and further clearly stated in his affidavit that the accident had been taken place as the driver of the milk tanker came from the opposite direction in a rash and negligent manner and hit to the motor cycle and deceased Imran Pasha was dragged approximately 30 meters along with his motor cycle.
Though PW-2 was cross examined at length, but nothing worth was elicited from his mouth in favour of the respondent.
Ont he other hand, PW-2 has categorically denied that the accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligency of the deceased.
Further the petitioners has examined Boregowda who is an eye witness as per the charge sheet.

PW-3 has clearly stated that he has received the summons from the Hon'ble court, but he is not aware of any facts and Zareena Taj vs Sudha.S on 5 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158579130/

but he has seen the accident in question and he was not at all present in spot of accident when the accident has been taken place and he do not have any property nearby the spot of accident and police have falsely implicated him as an eye witness and he has not given any statement before the police nor they have enquired him anything and he has not signed the papers and given any statement before the police.

18. Apart from this, on perusal of Ex-P3 spot mahazar, it is clearly stated that -

Thus it is clear that the accident had been taken place on the left side of the road proceeding from Tumkur towards Gubbi which clearly demonstrate that the accident has been taken place as the driver of the milk tanker came to his right side of the road who was coming from the Gubbi towards Tumkur and due to his negligence, accident has been taken place.

Thus evidence of the PW-1 eye witness and PW-2 another eye witness coupled with the Ex-P3 spot mahazar and Ex-P1 and 2 FIR and the complaint, it is clearly established that accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the milk tanker and due to driving of lorry towards wrong direction.

It is pertinent to note here that the respondent has not at all denied and disputed the Ex-P1 FIR and spot mahazar Ex-P3 which clearly shows that accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the milk tanker.

20. Further though respondent contended that PW-2 himself has given the further statement before the police stating that accident had been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the deceased Imran Pasha himself and accordingly after the investigation police has filed the charge sheet against the deceased Imran Pasha.
But no such further statement alleged to be given by the PW-2 is produced before the court.
Moreover the alleged statement if any cannot be believed and considered.
As the said statement alleged to be made is made before the police in view of Sec.24 of the erstwhile evidence Act.
Mere based on the alleged restatement given by the PW-2, this court cannot come to the conclusion that accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the deceased Imran Pasha.
Even neither of respondents has examined IO and also proved.

Moreover Ex-P2 the complaint lodged by the PW-2 immediately soon after the accident and the spot mahazar conducted by the police on the same day can be easily believed and accepted as it is was Zareena Taj vs Sudha.

6 made at the earliest point of time and there is no chances of any tampering.
In view of the above all discussions, it can be inferred that accident has been taken place due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the milk tanker.
Apart from this respondent No.2 has examined driver of milk tanker to prove their contention.
Driver of offending vehicle is material witness to state about cause and manner of accident.
The non-examination of driver of offending vehicle is fatal to case of respondent No.2.
As such adverse inference can be drawn against the driver of the offending vehicle with regard to rash and negligence.

21. At this juncture, It is necessary to apply the citation reported in AIR 2011 SC 1504 between Parmeshwari -vs- Amir Chand & Ors - wherein it has been held that - "In a situation of this nature, the Tribunal has rightly taken a holistic view of the matter.
It was necessary to be borne in mind that strict proof of an accident caused by a particular bus in a particular manner may not be possible to be done by the claimants.
The claimants were merely to establish their case on the touchstone of preponderance of probability.
The standard of proof beyond reasonable doubt could not have been applied."
22. Mere taking of defence is not sufficient to dislodge the testimony of other side, which has no sanctity in the eyes of Law.
Under such circumstances, the evidence of PW.1 which is supported by documents has to be accepted.
Consequently, I hold that the accident is proved to have been caused due to the actionable negligence of the driver of offending vehicle/milk tanker.

23. In addenda, in a claim for compensation U/Sec.166 of M.V Act, 1988, the claimant has to prove the incident only on preponderance of probabilities and proof beyond reasonable doubt is not required as held by the Hon'ble Apex Court in 'MANGALA RAM VS. ORIENTAL INSURANCE COMPANY reported in (2018) 5 SCC 656.

25. ISSUES NO.3: LOSS OF DEPENDENCY INCLUDING FUTURE PROSPECTS: From Ex-P7 Copy of DL of Imran Pasha, it reveals that date of birth of Imran Pasha is 07.06.1984 and as on the date of accident, Imran Pasha was aged 37 years.
Admittedly the deceased was bachelor and the appropriate multiplier as per Sarla Verma's case for the said age group of 36-40 is '15'.

The petitioner has not produced any documents regarding the avocation and income of Imran Pasha.
Hence notional income of the deceased Imran Pasha is taken as Rs.15,000/-p.m.

In a decision reported in 2018 ACJ 5 (Hem raj V/s Oriental Insurance Company Ltd & others),
the Hon'ble Apex Court held that addition on account of future prospects is admissible where minimum income is determined on guesswork in the absence of proof of income.

sentences.text: In the case on hand the deceased was aged 37 years.

As per dictum of Hon'ble Apex Court in AIR 2017 SCC 5157,
40% of income is to be added towards future prospects in case of self employed.

40% of Rs.15,000/-
works out to Rs.6,000/-.
Therefore the total income comes to Rs.21,000/- (15,000+6,000).

Admittedly, the deceased was bachelor and as such in view of the proposition of Law laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma's case, half of his income needs to be deducted towards personal & living expenses.
1/2 of Rs.21,000/- works out to Rs.10,500/-.
Income for consideration is Rs.10,500/- (21,000-10,500).
Annual income works out to Rs.1,26,000/- (10,500 X 12).
Appropriate multiplier is '15'.
Thus loss of dependency works out to Rs.18,90,000/- (1,26,000 X 15).
28. LOSS OF CONSORTIUM:

In view of the ratio laid by the Hon'ble Apex Court in (2021) 11 SCC 780 between United India Insurance Company Limited V/s. Satinder Kaur alias Satwinder Kaur and others, claimant is entitled to a sum of Rs.48,400/- (in view of the Pranay Sethi case, 10% of Rs.40,000/- has to be enhanced for every 3 years from 2017) on account of filial consortium and loss of love & affection.

31. The calculation table stands as follows :
1 Loss of Dependency : Rs.18,90,000-00 2 Loss of Consortium : 48,400-00 3 Loss of Estate : 18,150-00 4 Funeral Expenses : 18,150-00 Total Rs.19,74,700=00

Hence,
petitioners are entitle for compensation of Rs.19,74,700/-.

32. REGARDING INTEREST & LIABILITY: Having regard to the nature of the claim and current bank rate of interest, this Tribunal is of the view that if interest at the rate of 6% p.a, is awarded it would meet the ends of justice.

33. Therefore, the respondent No.1 being the RC owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer are liable to pay the aforesaid award amount to the petitioner together with interest @ 6% p.a. from the date of claim petition till realization of the entire amount.
However the respondent No.2 being the insurer of the offending vehicle is primarily liable to satisfy the award amount together with interest within one month from the date of this order.

Accordingly issue No.2 is answered as 'In the Affirmative' and issue No.3 is answered as 'Party in the affirmative'.
